title: Expose an ASP.NET Core endpoint
summary: Return the right status for a found or missing order from a minimal API.

scenario.briefing: The campus order endpoint always returns 200 with a placeholder string, even when the order does not exist. Return the order as JSON when found and a 404 when it is missing.

objectives.description: Map an order route to a handler with dependency injection.
Choose the status code for a missing resource.
Explain route binding, results, and dependency injection accurately.

hints: Ask the store for the order before building the response.
Return Results.NotFound when the store returns null.
Return Results.Ok with an object for the found case.

misconceptions.description: Returning a placeholder for a missing order.
misconceptions.feedback: A missing resource is a 404. Return Results.NotFound when the store finds nothing.

misconceptions.description: Returning 200 for a resource that does not exist.
misconceptions.feedback: 200 means the request succeeded with a representation. A missing resource should return 404.
The status code is part of the contract. Not found, validation failure, and server failure need different codes.

sections.title: Minimal APIs map routes to handlers
sections.body: WebApplication.CreateBuilder creates the host, and app.MapGet registers a handler for a route. Route values such as {id} bind to handler parameters by name. The handler returns an IResult that sets the status code and response body.

sections.title: Results express the outcome
sections.body: Results.Ok returns 200 with a body. Results.NotFound returns 404. A handler should choose the status from the domain outcome instead of returning 200 for every request. Typed results make the contract explicit and testable.

sections.title: Dependency injection reaches handlers
sections.body: Services registered on builder.Services are available as handler parameters or through constructor injection. Scoped services resolve per request. Keep the handler thin: validate input, call the service, and translate the result into an HTTP response.

steps.prompt: Edit Program.cs. The /orders/{id} handler resolves IOrderStore, returns Results.Ok with the order when found, and Results.NotFound when the store returns null.

steps.title: Choose the status
steps.prompt: A GET /orders/unknown request reaches the handler and the store returns null. Which status should the response use?

quiz.explanation: The request is valid but the resource does not exist. 404 communicates that outcome; 500 would blame the server for a normal miss.

hints: The route is valid but the resource is absent.
Choose the client-error status for a missing resource.
Do not use a server error for an expected miss.
